mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-46.0 to -40.6), indicating an established recovery momentum in discretionary shopping and recreation activity that should continue its upward trajectory over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -46.0 to -40.6 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite the prior three-week rising trend persisting unchanged.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp single-week drop in PARKS mobility (49.0 to 27.3) signals an abrupt weather or seasonal transition (e.g., end-of-summer rain or heat event) that reduces outdoor substitution and could redirect some activity toward indoor retail within one week, temporarily lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 49.0 to 27.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop exceeding 15 points, or PARKS rebounds without corresponding RETAIL_REC change.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-53 to -55) and WORKPLACES (-46) have both remained flat and deeply depressed for four weeks, jointly indicating stalled commuting recovery; the interaction of weak transit use and stagnant workplace attendance suppresses incidental retail trips tied to commuting routes, limiting RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain within 3 points of their 4-week average
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT held between -53.3 and -55.6 over four weeks
fact:WORKPLACES held between -45.9 and -46.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain flat and depressed.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has plateaued near 13-15 percent for four weeks, suggesting households have settled into a stable at-home behavioral baseline rather than continuing to reduce home-bound time; this behavioral saturation implies RETAIL_REC gains will plateau rather than keep accelerating over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed within 12.9 to 15.1 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise materially over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining flat, indicating behavioral saturation does not cap retail recovery.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed essentially flat (-18.3 to -20.4) while RETAIL_REC improved, indicating the RETAIL_REC gains are driven by genuine discretionary recovery rather than a shift from essential to non-essential spending; this decoupling should persist and support continued RETAIL_REC improvement over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within 3 points of its 4-week mean while RETAIL_REC changes by more than 3 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged narrowly between -18.3 and -20.4 while RETAIL_REC rose 5.4 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stalls or reverses even though GROCERY_PHARM remains flat, implying the decoupling signal has no predictive value.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained persistently suppressed below -53 for four straight weeks, consistent with ongoing public-transit capacity restrictions or rider caution tied to policy measures; sustained transit suppression constrains downstream retail trips reliant on transit access, holding RETAIL_REC below its pre-restriction trajectory over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50 for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged from -53.3 to -55.6 across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially over the next four weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -50 throughout, contradicting the suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The abrupt PARKS decline in the most recent week may reflect a one-off anomaly (e.g., a single rainy/hot day skewing the weekly mean) rather than a genuine seasonal regime shift; if PARKS rebounds in the following week, outdoor-indoor substitution effects on RETAIL_REC will be negligible, keeping RETAIL_REC direction driven mainly by its own momentum.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rebounds to within 5 points of its t-1w value within one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell sharply only in the most recent week after being stable at 43.7-49.0 for three prior weeks
failure_condition: PARKS does not rebound and instead continues declining, while RETAIL_REC also declines, suggesting a real sustained seasonal/outdoor shift rather than a one-off anomaly.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising RETAIL_REC and flat RESIDENTIAL/WORKPLACES suggests a steady-state regime where households have normalized routines around current restriction levels; in such a regime, incremental RETAIL_REC gains should slow and converge toward a stable equilibrium rather than continue compounding, especially if WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL stay unchanged.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES both varied by less than 2 points across four weeks while RETAIL_REC rose 5.4 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at a comparable or accelerating rate over the next two weeks despite RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES remaining unchanged, indicating no equilibrium convergence.
